item.title: 60 percent of EPF members have the potential to reach a basic savings level of RM390,000 by 2030 – Amir Hamzah

item.title: Hajiji dismisses divisive Borneo Bloc narrative, calls for cooperation to advance country
item.description: KOTA KINABALU (March 5): Sabah Chief Minister Datuk Seri Panglima Hajiji Noor has dismissed claims that Sabah and Sarawak are pursuing a political strategy known as the Borneo Bloc. item.title: Electronic waste processing factory raided, RM350,000 worth of goods seized
item.description: BUKIT MERTAJAM: Various electronic waste worth RM350,000 that was processed without permission was seized in a raid through Ops Hazard at a factory in the Asas Jaya Light Industrial Estate, here yesterday. Seberang Perai Tengah District Police Chief (SPT) ACP Helmi Aris said that in the raid at 1.30pm, a 44-year-old foreign man who was a worker at the factory involved was also arrested. item.title: Rice stocks are sufficient, fertilizer prices are being monitored – Mohamad Sabu
item.description: PUTRAJAYA: The government has assured that the country’s food supply, especially rice, is still at a stable level despite the conflict in West Asia raising concerns about the global supply chain. Minister of Agriculture and Food Security, Mohamad Sabu, said that so far the conflict has not affected the country’s food security because Malaysia is not dependent on countries in the Gulf region for food imports.
